title: NTT Data Spain runs OutSystems across five countries, so its low-code slot is a cross-border practice
content:
NTT Data Spain, the former everis, is recorded as active on OutSystems in Spain, the UK, Portugal, Belgium and Italy, with Microsoft and SAP alongside. Its verticals are banking, insurance and public sector.

Multi-country activity on one low-code platform is a stronger signal than a partner badge. It implies staff certified in five markets and references that travel between them, which is the kind of commitment the slot-occupancy criterion is designed to detect: the capability is institutional rather than account-specific, so displacing it means displacing a practice.

The same shape recurs across the tier-9 rows in Iberia and Benelux — Conclusion on Mendix and OutSystems, Valantic having acquired an OutSystems Elite partner, Valcon on Appian and Mendix. Proprietary low-code is the dominant occupant of precisely the slot a Powerhouse build would target, and in these firms it is an existing revenue line rather than an experiment. The row itself remains a mechanically rescored v2 entry with an OSS-portfolio screen outstanding.
